# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Jul 29, 2026)

## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on enhancing CI robustness, refining interop testing, and improving devstack reliability. Key achievements include fixing a critical deposit transaction bug and streamlining CI workflows for better efficiency and security.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Enhanced CI/CD Reliability and Security
Significant efforts were made to bolster the CI/CD pipeline. This included adding a feature to catch Rust tests that only compile via workspace feature unification ([#21501](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21501)), retrying `apt-get install` downloads to prevent transient failures ([#22083](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22083)), and implementing a diff-aware dependency review gate to flag critical vulnerabilities introduced by PRs ([#22079](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22079)). The Renovate setup was also converted to a reusable workflow with CVE baselining ([#22100](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22100)).

### Interoperability and Devstack Improvements
Interoperability testing received an upgrade with a new smoke test to verify transitive invalidation of cross-domain messages ([#22085](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22085)) and an update to exercise invalid messages on both chains in interop smoke tests ([#22074](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22074)). The devstack was refined by replacing the faucet/funder with a prefunded EOA ([#21706](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21706)) and configuring mutual trusted EL peering to improve resilience against peer drops ([#22052](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22052)).

### Critical Bug Fixes and Testing Updates
A crucial bug was addressed in the `CrossL2Inbox` contract to reject deposit transactions with a positive base fee and zero transaction gas price ([#21693](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21693)). Additionally, a flake in `op-reth` tests was fixed by ensuring the latest receipt proof state is waited for ([#21807](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21807)). The `op-node` registry test was updated to use `sepolia-devnet-2` ([#21990](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21990)).

### Operational Efficiency and Observability
Operational tasks included stopping the rebuilding of `op-program` and legacy Kona prestates to improve efficiency ([#22091](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22091)). The `op-supernode` also received improvements to clarify chain rewind observability with new metrics and logging ([#22088](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22088)).

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS

Eighteen new pull requests were opened today, covering a range of topics from documentation and tooling to core protocol enhancements. Notable PRs include:
- [#22120](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22120) adds reusable notice content type to documentation.
- [#22119](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22119) focuses on detecting malformed TODO issue references in the todo-checker.
- [#22118](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22118) and [#22117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22117) address `op-rbuilder` and `op-reth` builder configurations.
- [#22113](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22113) proposes bumping the reth dependency to a newer version.
- [#22109](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22109) and [#22108](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22108) are related to `op-reth` CLI surface snapshot tests and removal of an unsupported option.
- [#22106](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22106) aims to enhance lightnode reorg observability.
- [#22105](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22105) covers `kona-sp1` proposal safety in acceptance tests.
- [#22104](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22104) passes version to virtual node metrics in `op-supernode`.
- [#22102](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22102) and [#22101](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22101) gate `PostExec` transaction structure in batch validation and derivation respectively.
- [#22099](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22099) assigns cloud-security as the sole owner of CI and renovate files.
- [#22098](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22098) addresses inner `CREATE` warming in `alloy-op-evm`.
- [#22097](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22097) follows up on `kona-sp1-proposer` review nits.
- [#22096](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22096) and [#22095](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22095) are contract-bedrock updates for OPCM major version and resolving shared contract pause state.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Flaky Test Resolution
The long-standing flaky test `TestExecutePayloadSuccess` ([#19898](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19898)) was closed today. The issue was identified as a race condition where the `debug_executePayload` RPC on `op-reth` queried the proofs ExEx store before it had indexed the block. The fix involved waiting for the proofs ExEx store to be ready for the target block, specifically by waiting for the later of the two transaction receipt blocks before fetching account proofs.

## NEW ISSUES

### CI/Testing and Proposer Challenges
New issues highlight challenges in CI/testing and proposer logic. A flaky test `TestSequencerFailover_ConductorRPC` ([#22094](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22094)) is reported to hang and panic, indicating a potential issue in the conductor package. CI also faces an imbalance in `rust-cargo-hack` partitioning, leading to inefficient `rust-ci` runtimes ([#22103](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22103)). For proposers, questions arise regarding supporting fast finality mode ([#22112](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22112)) and which games the `kona-sp1-proposer` should defend when challenged ([#22111](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22111)). A new issue also notes that descendants of pending games can become canonical ([#22116](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22116)).

### ZK Devnet and Tooling Updates
A new issue outlines the need for a ZK devnet setup early in development to ensure an end-to-end working system ([#22110](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22110)). There's also a placeholder issue to update the `reth` dependency to versions 2.4.2 / 2.5.0 ([#22115](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22115)). Finally, a runbook for `op-deployer` and tooling is needed for PCD Milestone 3, addressing changes to the deployment pipeline and `intent.json` requirements ([#22114](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/22114)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### SDM Alpha/Beta Devnet Rollout ([#21273](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21273))
The discussion on rolling out an alpha/beta devnet for SDM (Superchain Data Model) is active. The latest update details the status, gap analysis, and plan. The `sdm-net-0` Sepolia alphanet spec has been merged, and the netchef CreateNetwork workflow is nearing completion. Key gaps identified include the lack of load generation tooling (compared to `kupcake spam`), the need for an SDM Grafana dashboard port, and the absence of a hot-enable/disable policy for SDM (requiring protocol code). The plan involves finishing the rollout, verifying SDM live functionality, standing up load, porting the dashboard, reviving the hot-toggle discussion with the Core team, and conducting baseline benchmarks. A risk was noted regarding `kona-node` CLs potentially not deriving post-exec transactions.
